newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX seen reaching new records above 2,800.
newsitem.headline: German DAX seen reaching new records above 2,800.

text.p: German shares were expected to continue to climb this week, boosted by strength in the dollar, which benefits German exporters, and gains in bourse newcomer Deutsche Telekom.

Dealers said a favourable technical picture for the DAX index of leading shares and buoyant stock markets worldwide provided the ideal environment for the DAX to decisively breach the 2,800 point level.
The IBIS DAX, measuring all-day computer dealings in the DAX index, was up 29.91 points at 2,799.38 by 1542 GMT, having earlier touched a a new record high of 2,805.75 points.
Dealers said the re-entry of the Italian lira into the European Exchange Rate Mechanism was also positive for German exporting stocks as it made monetary union seem more likely.
"The entry of the lira into the ERM makes the Euro seem more like a concrete reality," said one dealer.
Traders also said the strength in Deutsche Telekom shares, up 44 pfennigs at 32.90 marks in late IBIS trade, would also help the DAX index. The new stock had suffered some profit-taking last week.
"Players like how the shares stablised last week and are now ready to take positions," said one dealer.
Traders said in the absence of any significant economic data or company results on Tuesday, the market was more likely to be driven by technical factors.
Meanwhile, shares in Siemens were the only DAX stock to be in negative territory, falling 85 pfennigs, over one percent, to 70.55 marks.
Dealers said the stock was experiencing a delayed reaction to figures released last week at the computer unit of Siemens, Nixdorf Informationsssysteme AG.
